   152	/-! ## The residue of the chain, named -/
   153	
   154	variable (C π) in
   155	/-- **The shifted-datum presentation hypothesis** — the one link of the CHART-U(b) route of
   156	record that is not landed, stated exactly.
   157	
   158	Over an affine test `Spec A`, for a class `μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)` (in practice the
   159	twisted family `chartTwist C m Z _ λ` restricted to the test), a presentation is a
   160	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum` over `A` whose fibre witness predicate at every residue field agrees
   161	with the split witness predicate of `μ` at the corresponding point.
   162	
   163	Two remarks on the shape, both deliberate:
   164	
   165	* it is stated as an **agreement of predicates at every point**, not as a class equality.
   166	  That is weaker than "the datum's class is `μ`", and it is all the openness argument
   167	  consumes — which matters, because the class equality is what needs `cechPicClass_inv` and
   168	  a class-level identification, whereas a lane that can produce the pointwise agreement by any
   169	  other route may use this theorem immediately;
   170	* the split predicate is read at `Over.testPoint`, i.e. at the canonical residue-field point
   171	  of the affine test, so no choice of affine chart enters;
   172	* the `Algebra A (testPointField t)` / `IsScalarTower k A (testPointField t)` instances the
   173	  datum predicate needs are the **canonical** ones of `Picard/Pic0ChartTestPoint.lean`.  An
   174	  earlier draft of this file carried them as explicit `alg`/`tow` arguments; that was strictly
   175	  worse — it made the statement false for some regradings (`HasWitnessH1Vanishing` reads its
   176	  `Algebra` instance inside `relCurveMap`, so a non-canonical `alg` names a different set) as
   177	  well as unusable. -/
   178	def IsChartDatumPresentation {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   179	    (μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)) (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π) : Prop :=
   180	  ∀ t : (overSpec k A).left,
   181	    D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)
   182	      ↔ IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)
   183	
   184	/-! ## The carrier translation: `testPointField` on `Spec A` versus `Ideal.ResidueField`
   185	
   186	The engine's open set lives in `PrimeSpectrum A` and is indexed by `q.asIdeal.ResidueField`;
   187	`chartLocus` lives in `(overSpec k A).left = Spec A` and is indexed by `Over.testPointField`.
   188	The two carriers are the same space, but the two *fields* are only canonically isomorphic
   189	(mathlib's `Spec.residueFieldIso`), so the witness predicate has to be carried across that
   190	isomorphism.  That is what this section does, and it is the transport the (b-amendment) folds
   191	into "affine pieces glue by (V1c)-style locality". -/
   192	
   193	/-- **The residue-field comparison at a point of an affine test, as an algebra map.**
   194	
   195	`Over.testPointField t` is the *scheme* residue field `(Spec A).residueField t`, while every
   196	engine-facing predicate reads the *algebraic* residue field `t.asIdeal.ResidueField` of the
   197	prime.  Mathlib's `Spec.residueFieldIso` identifies them; this records the identification in
   198	the form the tower needs, namely that the canonical `A`-algebra structure on the scheme
   199	residue field (`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine`) factors through the algebraic one.
   200	
   201	Proof: both sides are `Spec.preimage` of a morphism out of `Spec κ(t)`, and `Spec.map` is
   202	injective on homs, so it suffices to compare after applying `Spec.map` — where the identity is
   203	mathlib's `Spec.map_residueFieldIso_inv_eq_fromSpecResidueField`. -/
   204	lemma algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine_factors {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   205	    (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
   206	    algebraMap A (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)
   207	      = ((Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of A) t).inv).hom.comp
   208	          (algebraMap A (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
   209	  rw [Over.algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine]
   210	  have h : Spec.preimage ((overSpec k A).left.fromSpecResidueField t)
   211	      = CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap A (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField)
   212	          ≫ (Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of A) t).inv := by
   213	    apply Spec.map_injective
   214	    rw [Spec.map_preimage, Spec.map_comp]
   215	    exact (Scheme.Spec.map_residueFieldIso_inv_eq_fromSpecResidueField (.of A) t).symm
   216	  rw [h]
   217	  rfl
   218	
   219	/-- **The witness predicate at a scheme-residue field agrees with the one at the prime's
   220	residue field, and the resulting locus is open.**
   221	
   222	`Over.testPointField t` is `(Spec A).residueField t` and the engine reads
   223	`t.asIdeal.ResidueField`; `Spec.residueFieldIso` identifies them, and the witness predicate
   224	transfers along any field extension in the `A`-tower
   225	(`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension`, `Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean:142`), in
   226	particular along an isomorphism.
   227	
   228	Three points about the proof, each of which was a suspected wall and is not:
   229	
   230	* the **carrier identification** `↥(overSpec k A).left = PrimeSpectrum A` is *definitional*
   231	  (`Scheme.Spec`'s carrier is `PrimeSpectrum` on the nose), so the two index sets need no
   232	  transport and the two topologies agree by `rfl`.  The set equality below is therefore a
   233	  pointwise `Iff`, not a homeomorphism argument;
   234	* the `Algebra A (testPointField t)` and `IsScalarTower k A (testPointField t)` instances the
   235	  predicate needs are **already canonical** (`Over.instAlgebraTestPointFieldAffine`,
   236	  `Over.instIsScalarTowerTestPointFieldAffine`), so nothing has to be passed in as an
   237	  argument.  An earlier draft of this file took `alg`/`tow` as explicit hypotheses and left
   238	  the conclusion as a `sorry`; that was a statement-shape artifact, not a gap — and worse,
   239	  the hypothesis form is *false for some regradings*, since an arbitrary `alg` need not be the
   240	  canonical instance and the predicate is not invariant under regrading the field over `A`;
   241	* the only genuine content is the transport across `Spec.residueFieldIso`, which is
   242	  `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension` applied to the isomorphism, in the tower
   243	  `A → κ(q) → (Spec A).residueField t` supplied by
   244	  `algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine_factors`. -/
   245	theorem isOpen_setOf_hasWitnessH1Vanishing_testPointField
   246	    (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom) {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   247	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π) :
   248	    IsOpen {t : (overSpec k A).left |
   249	      D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)} := by
   250	  -- The two loci are the SAME set of the SAME type: `↥(overSpec k A).left` is
   251	  -- `PrimeSpectrum A` definitionally, so only the fibre field differs, and the predicate is
   252	  -- invariant under the isomorphism between the two readings of it.
   253	  have hset : {t : (overSpec k A).left |
   254	        D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)}
   255	      = {q : PrimeSpectrum A |
   256	          ∃ W : ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left).CurveDivisor,
   257	            Scheme.CurveDivisor.picClass q.asIdeal.ResidueField W
   258	                = Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C A q.asIdeal.ResidueField)
   259	                    D.cechPicClass
   260	              ∧ Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule
   261	                  ((C ⊗ overSpec k q.asIdeal.ResidueField).left.divisorSheaf
   262	                    q.asIdeal.ResidueField W) 1)} := by
   263	    refine Set.ext fun t => ?_
   264	    -- the comparison iso as an algebra structure, and its tower over `A`
   265	    letI : Algebra (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField
   266	        (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
   267	      ((Scheme.Spec.residueFieldIso (.of A) t).inv).hom.toAlgebra
   268	    haveI : IsScalarTower A (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField
   269	        (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
   270	      IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq' (algebraMap_testPointFieldAffine_factors t)
   271	    exact (D.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension
   272	      (t : PrimeSpectrum A).asIdeal.ResidueField
   273	      (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)).symm
   274	  rw [hset]
   275	  exact D.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing hπ
   276	
   277	/-! ## Transports (0) and (iii): the identification with the landed locus -/
   278	
   279	/-- **`chartLocus` over an affine test is the witness locus of a presenting datum.**
   280	
   281	This is transport (0) (the class-indexation, landed as `cechWitnessLocus`) composed with
   282	transport (iii) (locality on the affine test, here trivial because the test *is* affine),
   283	run against the presentation hypothesis.  The content is entirely the translation between
   284	the two ways the tree indexes a fibre — by a point of the test object's space
   285	(`Over.testPoint`, the `chartLocus` side) and by a prime of the test algebra
   286	(`q.asIdeal.ResidueField`, the engine side).
   287	
   288	The translation is available precisely because `Over.testPointField` at a point of
   289	`(overSpec k A).left = Spec A` and `q.asIdeal.ResidueField` at the corresponding prime are
   290	the same field up to the canonical `Spec.residueFieldIso`, and the witness predicate is
   291	invariant under field isomorphism over the base (`hasWitnessH1Vanishing_iff_of_fieldExtension`
   292	applied to an isomorphism). -/
   293	theorem mem_chartLocus_iff_hasWitnessH1Vanishing
   294	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   295	    {μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)} {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π}
   296	    (hpres : IsChartDatumPresentation C π μ D) (t : (overSpec k A).left) :
   297	    IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)
   298	      ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t) :=
   299	  (hpres t).symm
   300	
   301	/-! ## The keystone, conditionally -/
   302	
   303	variable (C π) in
   304	/-- **`isOpen_chartLocus`, given the shifted-datum presentation** (dat-b row B-4's keystone,
   305	over an affine test).
   306	
   307	The proof is the route of record with the one missing link supplied as `hpres`: rewrite
   308	membership of `chartLocus` as the datum's witness predicate at the residue field of the
   309	point (the presentation), then quote the landed datum-level openness
   310	`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.isOpen_setOf_exists_witness_h1_vanishing` — itself the engine
   311	`datumRigidEngine_isOpen_vanishing` read through the GAP-6 dictionary.
   312	
   313	The general-test statement follows from this one by the affine-piece locality of the
   314	(b-amendment)'s transport (iii): `chartLocus` over `T` meets each affine open `U ⊆ T.left` in
   315	`chartLocus` over `Spec Γ(T.left, U)` (by `picEtMap_chartTwist` along
   316	`Over.fromSpecAffine T U`), and a set that is open in every member of an open cover is open.
   317	That last step is `isOpen_iff_forall_isOpen_inter`-style bookkeeping and needs no new
   318	mathematics; it is not stated here only because it would need the presentation hypothesis
   319	*per affine piece*, which is a statement about the general test and therefore belongs with
   320	the honesty/presentation obligations named in the header table. -/
   321	theorem isOpen_setOf_isSplitWitness_of_presentation (hπ : π ≫ P1.structureMap k = C.hom)
   322	    {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
   323	    {μ : picEt C (overSpec k A)} {D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C A π}
   324	    (hpres : IsChartDatumPresentation C π μ D) :
   325	    IsOpen {t : (overSpec k A).left |
   326	      IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)} := by
   327	  -- The engine's open set is indexed by primes of `A`; the locus is indexed by points of
   328	  -- `Spec A`.  These carriers are the same type, so the presentation rewrites one into the
   329	  -- other pointwise.
   330	  have hset : {t : (overSpec k A).left |
   331	        IsSplitWitness C (picEtMap C (Over.testPoint t) μ)}
   332	      = {t : (overSpec k A).left |
   333	          D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing (Over.testPointField (T := overSpec k A) t)} :=
   334	    Set.ext fun t => mem_chartLocus_iff_hasWitnessH1Vanishing hpres t
   335	  rw [hset]
   336	  exact isOpen_setOf_hasWitnessH1Vanishing_testPointField hπ D

    13	basic-open cocycle datum `D`; `Picard/Pic0ChartLocusFibreField.lean` proves that the witness
    14	predicate is intrinsic to the *fibre class* of the datum.  Both are stated per datum.  This
    15	file makes the step neither takes: it indexes the locus by a **class**.

    18	  with fibre class `c` has an effective witness divisor with vanishing `H¹` at `κ(q)`}`.

    30	`λ_t · θ^m · (−Σ)`; `informal/w4-datb-worksheet.md` §1.6 co-signs it with two binding

    61	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    62	variable {B : Type u} [CommRing B] [Algebra k B]
    63	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π]
    64	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]

    67	variable (π) in
    68	/-- **The witness locus of an untwisted class over an affine base**: the set of points of
    69	`Spec B` at which the fibre of the Čech class `c` admits an effective witness divisor with
    70	vanishing `H¹`.
    71	
    72	Stated over *classes*, not over data: a basic-open cocycle datum is a presentation, and the
    73	campaign's consumers index charts by a Picard class.  The ∀-quantifier is harmless because
    74	the predicate is class-intrinsic
    75	(`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq`) and every class is
    76	presented (`BasicOpenCocycleDatum.exists_cechPicClass_eq`) — see
    77	`mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_exists`.
    78	
    79	NOT the co-signed `chartLocus c λ` of `w4-datc` §3.3 / `w4-datb` §1.6: that one lives over a
    80	general test, is indexed by a plus class, and reads the TWISTED fibre class.  See the module
    81	header. -/
    82	def cechWitnessLocus (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) : Set (PrimeSpectrum B) :=
    83	  {q : PrimeSpectrum B | ∀ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
    84	    D.cechPicClass = c → D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing q.asIdeal.ResidueField}
    85	
    86	theorem mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff (c : (relCurve C B).CechPic) (q : PrimeSpectrum B) :
    87	    q ∈ cechWitnessLocus π c ↔ ∀ D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π,
    88	      D.cechPicClass = c → D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing q.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
    89	  Iff.rfl
    90	
    91	/-- **Membership is testable at any one presentation**: a datum `D` presenting `c` is a
    92	sound and complete test for membership of the witness locus.  This is the class-intrinsicity
    93	of the witness predicate, `hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq`, in the form
    94	the consumers use. -/
    95	theorem mem_cechWitnessLocus_iff_of_datum {c : (relCurve C B).CechPic}
    96	    (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π) (hD : D.cechPicClass = c) (q : PrimeSpectrum B) :
    97	    q ∈ cechWitnessLocus π c ↔ D.HasWitnessH1Vanishing q.asIdeal.ResidueField := by
    98	  refine ⟨fun h => h D hD, fun h D' hD' => ?_⟩
    99	  refine (D'.hasWitnessH1Vanishing_congr_of_cechPicClass_eq D
   100	    q.asIdeal.ResidueField ?_).mpr h
   101	  exact congrArg (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C B q.asIdeal.ResidueField))
   102	    (hD'.trans hD.symm)
   103	
   104	/-- **The ∀-form and the ∃-form of the witness locus agree**: every class is presented by

     8	public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.MorphismProperty.Limits
     9	
    10	/-!
    11	
    12	# Relatively representable morphisms
    13	
    14	In this file we define and develop basic results about relatively representable morphisms.
    15	
    16	Classically, a morphism `f : F ⟶ G` of presheaves is said to be representable if for any morphism
    17	`g : yoneda.obj X ⟶ G`, there exists a pullback square of the following form
    18	```
    19	  yoneda.obj Y --yoneda.map snd--> yoneda.obj X
    20	      |                                |
    21	     fst                               g
    22	      |                                |
    23	      v                                v
    24	      F ------------ f --------------> G
    25	```
    26	
    27	In this file, we define a notion of relative representability which works with respect to any
    28	functor, and not just `yoneda`. The fact that a morphism `f : F ⟶ G` between presheaves is
    29	representable in the classical case will then be given by `yoneda.relativelyRepresentable f`.
    30	
    31	## Main definitions
    32	
    33	Throughout this file, `F : C ⥤ D` is a functor between categories `C` and `D`.
    34	
    35	* `Functor.relativelyRepresentable`: A morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` in `D` is said to be relatively
    36	  representable with respect to `F`, if for any `g : F.obj a ⟶ Y`, there exists a pullback square
    37	  of the following form
    38	  ```
    39	  F.obj b --F.map snd--> F.obj a
    40	      |                     |
    41	     fst                    g
    42	      |                     |
    43	      v                     v
    44	      X ------- f --------> Y
    45	  ```
    46	
    47	* `MorphismProperty.relative`: Given a morphism property `P` in `C`, a morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` in `D`
    48	  satisfies `P.relative F` if it is relatively representable and for any `g : F.obj a ⟶ Y`, the
    49	  property `P` holds for any represented pullback of `f` by `g`.
    50	
    51	## API
    52	
    53	Given `hf : relativelyRepresentable f`, with `f : X ⟶ Y` and `g : F.obj a ⟶ Y`, we provide:
    54	* `hf.pullback g` which is the object in `C` such that `F.obj (hf.pullback g)` is a
    55	  pullback of `f` and `g`.
    56	* `hf.snd g` is the morphism `hf.pullback g ⟶ F.obj a`
    57	* `hf.fst g` is the morphism `F.obj (hf.pullback g) ⟶ X`
    58	* If `F` is full, and `f` is of type `F.obj c ⟶ G`, we also have `hf.fst' g : hf.pullback g ⟶ X`
    59	  which is the preimage under `F` of `hf.fst g`.
    60	* `hom_ext`, `hom_ext'`, `lift`, `lift'` are variants of the universal property of
    61	  `F.obj (hf.pullback g)`, where as much as possible has been formulated internally to `C`.
    62	  For these theorems we also need that `F` is full and/or faithful.
    63	* `symmetry` and `symmetryIso` are variants of the fact that pullbacks are symmetric for
    64	  representable morphisms, formulated internally to `C`. We assume that `F` is fully faithful here.
    65	
    66	We also provide some basic API for dealing with triple pullbacks, i.e. given
    67	`hf₁ : relativelyRepresentable f₁`, `f₂ : F.obj A₂ ⟶ X` and `f₃ : F.obj A₃ ⟶ X`, we define
    68	`hf₁.pullback₃ f₂ f₃` to be the pullback of `(A₁ ×_X A₂) ×_{A₁} (A₁ ×_X A₃)`. We then develop
    69	some API for working with this object, mirroring the usual API for pullbacks, but where as much
    70	as possible is phrased internally to `C`.
    71	
    72	## Main results
    73	
    74	* `relativelyRepresentable.isMultiplicative`: The class of relatively representable morphisms is
    75	  multiplicative.
    76	* `relativelyRepresentable.isStableUnderBaseChange`: Being relatively representable is stable under
    77	  base change.
    78	* `relativelyRepresentable.of_isIso`: Isomorphisms are relatively representable.
    79	
    80	-/
    81	
    82	@[expose] public section
    83	
    84	namespace CategoryTheory
    85	
    86	open Category Limits MorphismProperty
    87	
    88	universe v₁ v₂ u₁ u₂
    89	
    90	variable {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v₁} C] {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} D] (F : C ⥤ D)
    91	
    92	/-- A morphism `f : X ⟶ Y` in `D` is said to be relatively representable if for any
    93	`g : F.obj a ⟶ Y`, there exists a pullback square of the following form
    94	```
    95	F.obj b --F.map snd--> F.obj a
    96	    |                     |
    97	   fst                    g
    98	    |                     |
    99	    v                     v
   100	    X ------- f --------> Y
   101	```
   102	-/
   103	def Functor.relativelyRepresentable : MorphismProperty D :=
   104	  fun X Y f ↦ ∀ ⦃a : C⦄ (g : F.obj a ⟶ Y), ∃ (b : C) (snd : b ⟶ a)
   105	    (fst : F.obj b ⟶ X), IsPullback fst (F.map snd) f g
   106	
   107	namespace Functor.relativelyRepresentable
   108	
   109	section
   110	
   111	variable {F}
   112	variable {X Y : D} {f : X ⟶ Y} (hf : F.relativelyRepresentable f)
   113	  {b : C} {f' : F.obj b ⟶ Y} (hf' : F.relativelyRepresentable f')
   114	  {a : C} (g : F.obj a ⟶ Y) (hg : F.relativelyRepresentable g)
   115	
   116	/-- Let `f : X ⟶ Y` be a relatively representable morphism in `D`. Then, for any
   117	`g : F.obj a ⟶ Y`, `hf.pullback g` denotes the (choice of) a corresponding object in `C` such that
   118	there is a pullback square of the following form
   119	```
   120	hf.pullback g --F.map snd--> F.obj a
   121	    |                          |
   122	   fst                         g
   123	    |                          |
   124	    v                          v
   125	    X ---------- f ----------> Y
   126	``` -/
   127	noncomputable def pullback : C :=
   128	  (hf g).choose
   129	
   130	/-- Given a representable morphism `f : X ⟶ Y`, then for any `g : F.obj a ⟶ Y`, `hf.snd g`
   131	denotes the morphism in `C` giving rise to the following diagram
   132	```
   133	hf.pullback g --F.map (hf.snd g)--> F.obj a
   134	    |                                 |
   135	   fst                                g
   136	    |                                 |
   137	    v                                 v
   138	    X -------------- f -------------> Y
   139	``` -/
   140	noncomputable abbrev snd : hf.pullback g ⟶ a :=
   141	  (hf g).choose_spec.choose
   142	
   143	/-- Given a relatively representable morphism `f : X ⟶ Y`, then for any `g : F.obj a ⟶ Y`,
   144	`hf.fst g` denotes the first projection in the following diagram, given by the defining property
   145	of `f` being relatively representable
   146	```
   147	hf.pullback g --F.map (hf.snd g)--> F.obj a
   148	    |                                 |
   149	hf.fst g                              g
   150	    |                                 |
   151	    v                                 v
   152	    X -------------- f -------------> Y
   153	``` -/
   154	noncomputable abbrev fst : F.obj (hf.pullback g) ⟶ X :=
   155	  (hf g).choose_spec.choose_spec.choose
   156	
   157	/-- When `F` is full, given a representable morphism `f' : F.obj b ⟶ Y`, then `hf'.fst' g` denotes
   158	the preimage of `hf'.fst g` under `F`. -/
   159	noncomputable abbrev fst' [Full F] : hf'.pullback g ⟶ b :=
   160	  F.preimage (hf'.fst g)
   161	
   162	lemma map_fst' [Full F] : F.map (hf'.fst' g) = hf'.fst g :=
   163	  F.map_preimage _
   164	
   165	lemma isPullback : IsPullback (hf.fst g) (F.map (hf.snd g)) f g :=
   166	  (hf g).choose_spec.choose_spec.choose_spec
   167	
   168	@[reassoc]
   169	lemma w : hf.fst g ≫ f = F.map (hf.snd g) ≫ g := (hf.isPullback g).w
   170	
   171	/-- Variant of the pullback square when `F` is full, and given `f' : F.obj b ⟶ Y`. -/
   172	lemma isPullback' [Full F] : IsPullback (F.map (hf'.fst' g)) (F.map (hf'.snd g)) f' g :=
   173	  (hf'.map_fst' _) ▸ hf'.isPullback g
   174	
   175	@[reassoc]
   176	lemma w' {X Y Z : C} {f : X ⟶ Z} (hf : F.relativelyRepresentable (F.map f)) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
   177	    [Full F] [Faithful F] : hf.fst' (F.map g) ≫ f = hf.snd (F.map g) ≫ g :=
   178	  F.map_injective <| by simp [(hf.w (F.map g))]
   179	
   180	lemma isPullback_of_map {X Y Z : C} {f : X ⟶ Z} (hf : F.relativelyRepresentable (F.map f))
   181	    (g : Y ⟶ Z) [Full F] [Faithful F] :
   182	    IsPullback (hf.fst' (F.map g)) (hf.snd (F.map g)) f g :=
   183	  IsPullback.of_map F (hf.w' g) (hf.isPullback' (F.map g))
   184	
   185	variable {g}
   186	
   187	/-- Two morphisms `a b : c ⟶ hf.pullback g` are equal if
   188	* Their compositions (in `C`) with `hf.snd g : hf.pullback  ⟶ X` are equal.
   189	* The compositions of `F.map a` and `F.map b` with `hf.fst g` are equal. -/
   190	@[ext 100]
   191	lemma hom_ext [Faithful F] {c : C} {a b : c ⟶ hf.pullback g}
   192	    (h₁ : F.map a ≫ hf.fst g = F.map b ≫ hf.fst g)
   193	    (h₂ : a ≫ hf.snd g = b ≫ hf.snd g) : a = b :=
   194	  F.map_injective <|
   195	    PullbackCone.IsLimit.hom_ext (hf.isPullback g).isLimit h₁ (by simpa using! F.congr_map h₂)
   196	
   197	/-- In the case of a representable morphism `f' : F.obj Y ⟶ G`, whose codomain lies
   198	in the image of `F`, we get that two morphism `a b : Z ⟶ hf.pullback g` are equal if
   199	* Their compositions (in `C`) with `hf'.snd g : hf.pullback  ⟶ X` are equal.
   200	* Their compositions (in `C`) with `hf'.fst' g : hf.pullback  ⟶ Y` are equal. -/
   201	@[ext]
   202	lemma hom_ext' [Full F] [Faithful F] {c : C} {a b : c ⟶ hf'.pullback g}
   203	    (h₁ : a ≫ hf'.fst' g = b ≫ hf'.fst' g)
   204	    (h₂ : a ≫ hf'.snd g = b ≫ hf'.snd g) : a = b :=
   205	  hf'.hom_ext (by simpa [map_fst'] using F.congr_map h₁) h₂
   206	
   207	section
   208	
   209	variable {c : C} (i : F.obj c ⟶ X) (h : c ⟶ a) (hi : i ≫ f = F.map h ≫ g)
   210	
   211	/-- The lift (in `C`) obtained from the universal property of `F.obj (hf.pullback g)`, in the
   212	case when the cone point is in the image of `F.obj`. -/
   213	noncomputable def lift [Full F] : c ⟶ hf.pullback g :=
   214	  F.preimage <| PullbackCone.IsLimit.lift (hf.isPullback g).isLimit _ _ hi
   215	
   216	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
   217	lemma lift_fst [Full F] : F.map (hf.lift i h hi) ≫ hf.fst g = i := by
   218	  simpa [lift] using! PullbackCone.IsLimit.lift_fst _ _ _ _
   219	
   220	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
   221	lemma lift_snd [Full F] [Faithful F] : hf.lift i h hi ≫ hf.snd g = h :=
   222	  F.map_injective <| by simpa [lift] using! PullbackCone.IsLimit.lift_snd _ _ _ _
   223	
   224	end
   225	
   226	section
   227	
   228	variable {c : C} (i : c ⟶ b) (h : c ⟶ a) (hi : F.map i ≫ f' = F.map h ≫ g)
   229	
   230	/-- Variant of `lift` in the case when the domain of `f` lies in the image of `F.obj`. Thus,
   231	in this case, one can obtain the lift directly by giving two morphisms in `C`. -/
   232	noncomputable def lift' [Full F] : c ⟶ hf'.pullback g := hf'.lift _ _ hi
   233	
   234	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
   235	lemma lift'_fst [Full F] [Faithful F] : hf'.lift' i h hi ≫ hf'.fst' g = i :=
   236	  F.map_injective (by simp [lift'])
   237	
   238	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
   239	lemma lift'_snd [Full F] [Faithful F] : hf'.lift' i h hi ≫ hf'.snd g = h := by
   240	  simp [lift']
   241	
   242	end
   243	
   244	/-- Given two representable morphisms `f' : F.obj b ⟶ Y` and `g : F.obj a ⟶ Y`, we
   245	obtain an isomorphism `hf'.pullback g ⟶ hg.pullback f'`. -/
   246	noncomputable def symmetry [Full F] : hf'.pullback g ⟶ hg.pullback f' :=
   247	  hg.lift' (hf'.snd g) (hf'.fst' g) (hf'.isPullback' _).w.symm
   248	
   249	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
   250	lemma symmetry_fst [Full F] [Faithful F] : hf'.symmetry hg ≫ hg.fst' f' = hf'.snd g := by
   251	  simp [symmetry]
   252	
   253	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
   254	lemma symmetry_snd [Full F] [Faithful F] : hf'.symmetry hg ≫ hg.snd f' = hf'.fst' g := by
   255	  simp [symmetry]
   256	
   257	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
   258	lemma symmetry_symmetry [Full F] [Faithful F] : hf'.symmetry hg ≫ hg.symmetry hf' = 𝟙 _ :=
   259	  hom_ext' hf' (by simp) (by simp)
   260	
   261	/-- The isomorphism given by `Presheaf.representable.symmetry`. -/
   262	@[simps]
   263	noncomputable def symmetryIso [Full F] [Faithful F] : hf'.pullback g ≅ hg.pullback f' where
   264	  hom := hf'.symmetry hg
   265	  inv := hg.symmetry hf'
   266	
   267	instance [Full F] [Faithful F] : IsIso (hf'.symmetry hg) :=
   268	  (hf'.symmetryIso hg).isIso_hom
   269	
   270	end
   271	
   272	/-- When `C` has pullbacks, then `F.map f` is representable with respect to `F` for any
   273	`f : a ⟶ b` in `C`. -/
   274	lemma map [Full F] [HasPullbacks C] {a b : C} (f : a ⟶ b)
   275	    [∀ c (g : c ⟶ b), PreservesLimit (cospan f g) F] :
   276	    F.relativelyRepresentable (F.map f) := fun c g ↦ by
   277	  obtain ⟨g, rfl⟩ := F.map_surjective g
   278	  refine ⟨Limits.pullback f g, Limits.pullback.snd f g, F.map (Limits.pullback.fst f g), ?_⟩
   279	  apply F.map_isPullback <| IsPullback.of_hasPullback f g
   280	
   281	lemma of_isIso {X Y : D} (f : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso f] : F.relativelyRepresentable f :=
   282	  fun a g ↦ ⟨a, 𝟙 a, g ≫ CategoryTheory.inv f, IsPullback.of_vert_isIso ⟨by simp⟩⟩
   283	
   284	lemma isomorphisms_le : MorphismProperty.isomorphisms D ≤ F.relativelyRepresentable :=
   285	  fun _ _ f hf ↦ letI : IsIso f := hf; of_isIso F f
   286	
   287	instance isMultiplicative : IsMultiplicative F.relativelyRepresentable where
   288	  id_mem _ := of_isIso F _
   289	  comp_mem {F G H} f g hf hg := fun X h ↦
   290	    ⟨hf.pullback (hg.fst h), hf.snd (hg.fst h) ≫ hg.snd h, hf.fst (hg.fst h),
   291	      by simpa using IsPullback.paste_vert (hf.isPullback (hg.fst h)) (hg.isPullback h)⟩
   292	
   293	instance isStableUnderBaseChange : IsStableUnderBaseChange F.relativelyRepresentable where
   294	  of_isPullback {X Y Y' X' f g f' g'} P₁ hg a h := by
   295	    refine ⟨hg.pullback (h ≫ f), hg.snd (h ≫ f), ?_, ?_⟩
   296	    · apply P₁.lift (hg.fst (h ≫ f)) (F.map (hg.snd (h ≫ f)) ≫ h) (by simpa using hg.w (h ≫ f))
   297	    · apply IsPullback.of_right' (hg.isPullback (h ≫ f)) P₁
   298	
   299	instance respectsIso : RespectsIso F.relativelyRepresentable :=
   300	  (isStableUnderBaseChange F).respectsIso

1	/-

     5	-/
     6	module
     7	
     8	public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Elementwise
     9	public import Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Types.Basic
    10	public import Mathlib.Data.Set.Lattice.Image
    11	
    12	/-!
    13	
    14	# Subfunctor of types
    15	
    16	We define subfunctors of a type-valued functors.
    17	
    18	## Main definition
    19	
    20	`CategoryTheory.Subfunctor` : A subfunctor of a type-valued functor.
    21	
    22	-/
    23	
    24	@[expose] public section
    25	
    26	
    27	universe w v u
    28	
    29	open Opposite CategoryTheory ConcreteCategory
    30	
    31	namespace CategoryTheory
    32	
    33	variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    34	
    35	/-- A subfunctor of a functor consists of a subset of `F.obj U` for every `U`,
    36	compatible with the restriction maps `F.map i`. -/
    37	@[ext]
    38	structure Subfunctor (F : C ⥤ Type w) where
    39	  /-- If `G` is a subfunctor of `F`, then the sections of `G` on `U` forms a subset of sections of
    40	  `F` on `U`. -/
    41	  obj : ∀ U, Set (F.obj U)
    42	  /-- If `G` is a subfunctor of `F` and `i : U ⟶ V`, then for each `G`-sections on `U` `x`,
    43	  `F i x` is in `F(V)`. -/
    44	  map : ∀ {U V : C} (i : U ⟶ V), obj U ⊆ F.map i ⁻¹' obj V
    45	
    46	@[deprecated (since := "2025-12-11")] alias Subpresheaf := Subfunctor
    47	
    48	variable {F F' F'' : C ⥤ Type w} (G G' : Subfunctor F)
    49	
    50	instance : PartialOrder (Subfunctor F) :=
    51	  PartialOrder.lift Subfunctor.obj (fun _ _ => Subfunctor.ext)
    52	
    53	instance : CompleteLattice (Subfunctor F) where
    54	  sup F G :=
    55	    { obj U := F.obj U ⊔ G.obj U
    56	      map _ _ := by
    57	        rintro (h | h)
    58	        · exact Or.inl (F.map _ h)
    59	        · exact Or.inr (G.map _ h) }
    60	  le_sup_left _ _ _ := by simp
    61	  le_sup_right _ _ _ := by simp
    62	  sup_le F G H h₁ h₂ U := by
    63	    rintro x (h | h)
    64	    · exact h₁ _ h
    65	    · exact h₂ _ h
    66	  inf S T :=
    67	    { obj U := S.obj U ⊓ T.obj U
    68	      map _ _ h := ⟨S.map _ h.1, T.map _ h.2⟩}
    69	  inf_le_left _ _ _ _ h := h.1
    70	  inf_le_right _ _ _ _ h := h.2
    71	  le_inf _ _ _ h₁ h₂ _ _ h := ⟨h₁ _ h, h₂ _ h⟩
    72	  sSup S :=
    73	    { obj U := sSup (Set.image (fun T ↦ T.obj U) S)
    74	      map f x hx := by
    75	        obtain ⟨_, ⟨F, h, rfl⟩, h'⟩ := hx
    76	        simp only [Set.sSup_eq_sUnion, Set.sUnion_image, Set.preimage_iUnion,
    77	          Set.mem_iUnion, Set.mem_preimage, exists_prop]
    78	        exact ⟨_, h, F.map f h'⟩ }
    79	  isLUB_sSup _ := ⟨fun _ _ _ _ ↦ by aesop, fun _ _ _ ↦ by aesop⟩
    80	  sInf S :=
    81	    { obj U := sInf (Set.image (fun T ↦ T.obj U) S)
    82	      map f x hx := by
    83	        rintro _ ⟨F, h, rfl⟩
    84	        exact F.map f (hx _ ⟨_, h, rfl⟩) }
    85	  isGLB_sInf _ := ⟨fun _ _ _ _ ↦ by aesop, fun _ _ _ ↦ by aesop⟩
    86	  bot :=
    87	    { obj U := ⊥
    88	      map := by simp }
    89	  bot_le _ _ := bot_le
    90	  top :=
    91	    { obj U := ⊤
    92	      map := by simp }
    93	  le_top _ _ := le_top
    94	
    95	namespace Subfunctor
    96	
    97	lemma le_def (S T : Subfunctor F) : S ≤ T ↔ ∀ U, S.obj U ≤ T.obj U := Iff.rfl
    98	
    99	variable (F)
   100	
   101	@[simp] lemma top_obj (i : C) : (⊤ : Subfunctor F).obj i = ⊤ := rfl
   102	@[simp] lemma bot_obj (i : C) : (⊥ : Subfunctor F).obj i = ⊥ := rfl
   103	
   104	variable {F}
   105	
   106	lemma sSup_obj (S : Set (Subfunctor F)) (U : C) :
   107	    (sSup S).obj U = sSup (Set.image (fun T ↦ T.obj U) S) := rfl
   108	
   109	lemma sInf_obj (S : Set (Subfunctor F)) (U : C) :
   110	    (sInf S).obj U = sInf (Set.image (fun T ↦ T.obj U) S) := rfl
   111	
   112	@[simp]
   113	lemma iSup_obj {ι : Sort*} (S : ι → Subfunctor F) (U : C) :
   114	    (⨆ i, S i).obj U = ⋃ i, (S i).obj U := by
   115	  simp [iSup, sSup_obj]
   116	
   117	@[simp]
   118	lemma iInf_obj {ι : Sort*} (S : ι → Subfunctor F) (U : C) :
   119	    (⨅ i, S i).obj U = ⋂ i, (S i).obj U := by
   120	  simp [iInf, sInf_obj]
   121	
   122	@[simp]
   123	lemma max_obj (S T : Subfunctor F) (i : C) :
   124	    (S ⊔ T).obj i = S.obj i ∪ T.obj i := rfl
   125	
   126	@[simp]
   127	lemma min_obj (S T : Subfunctor F) (i : C) :
   128	    (S ⊓ T).obj i = S.obj i ∩ T.obj i := rfl
   129	
   130	lemma max_min (S₁ S₂ T : Subfunctor F) :
   131	    (S₁ ⊔ S₂) ⊓ T = (S₁ ⊓ T) ⊔ (S₂ ⊓ T) := by
   132	  aesop
   133	
   134	lemma iSup_min {ι : Sort*} (S : ι → Subfunctor F) (T : Subfunctor F) :
   135	    (⨆ i, S i) ⊓ T = ⨆ i, S i ⊓ T := by
   136	  aesop
   137	
   138	instance : Nonempty (Subfunctor F) :=
   139	  inferInstance
   140	
   141	/-- The subfunctor as a functor. -/
   142	@[simps obj map]
   143	def toFunctor : C ⥤ Type w where
   144	  obj U := G.obj U
   145	  map i := ↾fun x => ⟨F.map i x, G.map i x.prop⟩
   146	
   147	instance {U} : CoeHead (G.toFunctor.obj U) (F.obj U) where
   148	  coe := Subtype.val
   149	
   150	/-- The inclusion of a subfunctor to the original functor. -/
   151	@[simps]
   152	def ι : G.toFunctor ⟶ F where app _ := ↾fun x ↦ x
   153	
   154	instance : Mono G.ι :=
   155	  ⟨@fun _ _ _ e =>
   156	    NatTrans.ext <| funext fun U => hom_ext _ _ fun x => Subtype.ext <| congr_hom (congr_app e U) x⟩
   157	
   158	/-- The inclusion of a subfunctor to a larger subfunctor -/
   159	@[simps]
   160	def homOfLe {G G' : Subfunctor F} (h : G ≤ G') : G.toFunctor ⟶ G'.toFunctor where
   161	  app U := ↾fun x ↦ ⟨x, h U x.prop⟩
   162	
   163	instance {G G' : Subfunctor F} (h : G ≤ G') : Mono (Subfunctor.homOfLe h) :=
   164	  ⟨fun _ _ e => NatTrans.ext <| funext fun U => hom_ext _ _ fun x => by
   165	    exact Subtype.ext (congr_arg Subtype.val <| (congr_hom (congr_app e U) x) :)⟩
   166	
   167	@[reassoc (attr := simp)]
   168	theorem homOfLe_ι {G G' : Subfunctor F} (h : G ≤ G') :
   169	    Subfunctor.homOfLe h ≫ G'.ι = G.ι := by
   170	  ext
   171	  rfl
   172	
   173	instance : IsIso (Subfunctor.ι (⊤ : Subfunctor F)) := by
   174	  refine @NatIso.isIso_of_isIso_app _ _ _ _ _ _ _ ?_
   175	  intro X
   176	  rw [isIso_iff_bijective]
   177	  exact ⟨Subtype.coe_injective, fun x => ⟨⟨x, _root_.trivial⟩, rfl⟩⟩
   178	
   179	theorem eq_top_iff_isIso : G = ⊤ ↔ IsIso G.ι := by
   180	  constructor
   181	  · rintro rfl

    14

    17	define `G'.image p : Subfunctor F` as the image of `G'` by `f`, and

    34	/-- The range of a morphism of type-valued functors, as a subfunctor of the target. -/

    37	  obj U := Set.range (p.app U)
    38	  map := by

    40	    exact ⟨_, NatTrans.naturality_apply p i x⟩

    44	
    45	set_option backward.defeqAttrib.useBackward true in

+/-

+Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
+Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
+-/
+import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.FiniteDimensional.Basic
+import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.TensorProduct.RightExactness
+
+/-!
+# Rank-one fibre quotients
+
+If a vector `1 ⊗ s` is nonzero in a one-dimensional fibre `K ⊗[B] M`, then it spans that
+fibre.  Consequently, every surjective image of `M` that kills `s` has zero `K`-fibre.
+
+The mapped-submodule form is tailored to an ideal `J ≤ B`: if the fibre of `J` has rank one,
+`s ∈ J` survives in that fibre, and a quotient map kills `s`, then the image of `J` in the
+quotient has zero residue-field fibre.  This is purely right exactness of tensor product;
+neither flatness nor finite generation over `B` is needed at this step.
+-/
+
+set_option autoImplicit false
+
+universe u
+
+open scoped TensorProduct
+
+namespace AlgebraicGeometry
+
+namespace RankOneFibre
+
+/-- A surjective image of a module has zero field fibre if it kills a nonzero vector spanning
+the one-dimensional source fibre. -/
+theorem subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_finrank_eq_one
+    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
+    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
+    (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (hf : Function.Surjective f) (s : M)
+    (hfin : Module.finrank K (K ⊗[B] M) = 1)
+    (hs : (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s ≠ 0) (hfs : f s = 0) :
+    Subsingleton (N ⊗[B] K) := by
+  have hft : Function.Surjective (f.lTensor K) :=
+    LinearMap.lTensor_surjective K hf
+  have hzero : ∀ v : K ⊗[B] M, (f.lTensor K) v = 0 := by
+    intro v
+    obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := exists_smul_eq_of_finrank_eq_one hfin hs v
+    rw [← hc, ← TensorProduct.tmul_eq_smul_one_tmul c s,
+      LinearMap.lTensor_tmul, hfs]
+    simp
+  have hsub : Subsingleton (K ⊗[B] N) := by
+    refine ⟨fun x y => ?_⟩
+    obtain ⟨x', rfl⟩ := hft x
+    obtain ⟨y', rfl⟩ := hft y
+    rw [hzero x', hzero y']
+  exact (TensorProduct.comm B N K).toEquiv.subsingleton
+
+/-- If a linear map kills a generator of a one-dimensional source fibre, the fibre of its
+range is zero. -/
+theorem subsingleton_range_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
+    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
+    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
+    (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (s : M)
+    (hfin : Module.finrank K (K ⊗[B] M) = 1)
+    (hs : (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s ≠ 0) (hfs : f s = 0) :
+    Subsingleton ((LinearMap.range f) ⊗[B] K) := by
+  apply subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_finrank_eq_one f.rangeRestrict
+    (LinearMap.surjective_rangeRestrict f) s hfin hs
+  apply Subtype.ext
+  exact hfs
+
+/-- Let `P` be a submodule whose field fibre is one-dimensional.  If `s ∈ P` survives in
+that fibre and `f s = 0`, then the fibre of the image `f(P)` is zero.
+
+For a chart ideal `J` and the quotient map `B → B/(s)`, the conclusion is precisely the
+vanishing of the fibre of the image of `J` in `B/(s)`. -/
+theorem subsingleton_map_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
+    {B K M N : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
+    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module B N]
+    (P : Submodule B M) (f : M →ₗ[B] N) (s : M) (hsP : s ∈ P)
+    (hfin : Module.finrank K (K ⊗[B] P) = 1)
+    (hs : (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] (⟨s, hsP⟩ : P) ≠ 0) (hfs : f s = 0) :
+    Subsingleton ((P.map f) ⊗[B] K) := by
+  rw [← LinearMap.range_domRestrict P f]
+  apply subsingleton_range_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
+    (f.domRestrict P) (⟨s, hsP⟩ : P) hfin hs
+  simpa using hfs
+
+/-- Quotienting by a vector that survives and spans a one-dimensional field fibre produces
+a quotient with zero field fibre. -/
+theorem subsingleton_quotient_span_tensor_of_finrank_eq_one
+    {B K M : Type u} [CommRing B] [Field K] [Algebra B K]
+    [AddCommGroup M] [Module B M]
+    (s : M) (hfin : Module.finrank K (K ⊗[B] M) = 1)
+    (hs : (1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B] s ≠ 0) :
+    Subsingleton ((M ⧸ Submodule.span B ({s} : Set M)) ⊗[B] K) := by
+  apply subsingleton_tensor_of_surjective_of_finrank_eq_one
+    (Submodule.span B ({s} : Set M)).mkQ
+    (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _) s hfin hs
+  rw [Submodule.mkQ_apply, Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
+  exact Submodule.mem_span_singleton_self s
+
+end RankOneFibre
+
+end AlgebraicGeometry

+  simpa using hfs
+

+/-!
+# Rank-one fibre reduction for the chart colength
+
+This is the geometric wrapper around `RankOneFibre`: the genuine chart-reading ideal is mapped
+to `B/(read s)`, and that image is definitionally `chartIdealColengthModule`.  Thus a pointwise
+span statement for the fibre of the ideal immediately gives the desired vanishing of the
+colength fibre.  The span statement is allowed to include the zero-fibre case.
+-/
+
+set_option autoImplicit false
+set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
+
+universe u
+
+open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite
+open scoped TensorProduct
+
+namespace AlgebraicGeometry
+
+attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
+
+variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
+variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
+variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] {a : ℕ}
+
+namespace ThetaGeneratorSeed
+
+/-- **Pointwise chart-colength fibre vanishing from ideal-fibre span.**  Let `B` be the
+pinned-chart section ring, `J` the genuine `B`-ideal generated by the readings of `K`, and
+`I = (read s)` for `s ∈ K`.  If every vector of
+`κ(p) ⊗[B] J` is a scalar multiple of `1 ⊗ read(s)`, then the image of `J` in `B/I` has
+zero `κ(p)`-fibre.  This is the exact single-point input consumed by the `κ(z)` RD-N bridge;
+it uses no global base-fibre or flatness inference. -/
+theorem subsingleton_chartIdealColengthModule_tensor_residueField_of_ideal_span
+    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) (b : Bool)
+    (s : relThetaSections C R π a) (hsK : s ∈ K)
+    (p : PrimeSpectrum Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b))
+    (hspan : ∀ v : p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[
+        Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)]
+        (chartReadIdeal K b), ∃ c : p.asIdeal.ResidueField,
+          c • ((1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ⊗ₜ[
+            Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)]
+            (⟨relThetaResSide a b (le_rfl) s,
+              by
+                exact Ideal.subset_span ⟨⟨s, hsK⟩, rfl⟩⟩ :
+              chartReadIdeal K b)) = v) :
+    Subsingleton ((chartIdealColengthModule K b s) ⊗[
+      Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) := by
+  let B : Type u := Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)
+  let I : Ideal B := Ideal.span {relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s}
+  let P : Submodule B B := chartReadIdeal K b
+  let f : B →ₗ[B] (B ⧸ I) := (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ B I).toLinearMap
+  have hsP : relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s ∈ P := by
+    exact Ideal.subset_span ⟨⟨s, hsK⟩, rfl⟩
+  have hfs : f (relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s) = 0 := by
+    change Ideal.Quotient.mk I (relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s) = 0
+    exact Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr (Ideal.subset_span (by simp))
+  have hzero := RankOneFibre.subsingleton_map_tensor_of_span_singleton
+    P f (relThetaResSide a b le_rfl s) hsP (by
+      intro v
+      exact hspan v) hfs
+  change Subsingleton ((P.map f) ⊗[B] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) at hzero
+  exact hzero
+
+end ThetaGeneratorSeed
+
+end AlgebraicGeometry
